issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee cannot execute a conditional personal decree against a mortgagor’s other property before first pursuing recovery through the statutory compensation that replaces the vested mortgaged estate.
material_facts: The entire property securing the mortgage was an estate that had vested in the State.
The decree made personal liability conditional on the mortgage debt remaining unsatisfied after recourse to the mortgaged property.
The mortgagees had submitted a claim under the statutory scheme, and the Claims Officer had determined an amount payable from the compensation for the estate.
The mortgagees sought to execute the personal decree against the mortgagor’s other property without first recovering the determined amount through the compensation scheme.
issues.conclusion: Execution against the mortgagor’s other property was incompetent at that stage. The mortgagees had first to seek recovery from the compensation payable for the vested estate; personal execution could follow only if that recovery did not satisfy the decree. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4(d) of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, proceedings for recovery of mortgage debt secured by an estate are barred in the circumstances governed by the Act. Sections 14–18 establish the process for notifying, determining, and finally adjudicating secured-creditor claims, while section 24(5) directs payment of the determined mortgage amount from compensation. Together, these provisions create an integrated statutory process that must be pursued before ordinary execution of a conditional personal decree. The compensation operates as substituted security, consistently with the principle reflected in section 73(2) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and the sequence also accords with Order 34 Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Court considered Lion Insurance Association Ltd. v. Tucker but found it did not assist the creditor’s construction; it distinguished Raghubir v. Basudevanand and Mahanth Sukhdeo Das v. Kashi Prasad Tiwari as involving materially different property circumstances, and found it unnecessary to decide the point raised from Rana Sheo Ambar Singh v. The Allahabad Bank Ltd.

rule.if: execution_of_personal_mortgage_decree and entire_mortgaged_estate_vested and personal_recourse_conditional_on_security_shortfall and compensation_claim_determined and compensation_recovery_not_exhausted

predicates.execution_of_personal_mortgage_decree: A creditor is seeking to enforce a personal decree arising from a mortgage.
predicates.entire_mortgaged_estate_vested: All property securing the mortgage has vested in the State, leaving none of that property with the mortgagor.
predicates.personal_recourse_conditional_on_securit: The decree permits recourse to the mortgagor personally only if recovery from the secured property does not satisfy the debt.
predicates.compensation_claim_determined: The creditor’s claim has been determined for payment from compensation payable in place of the vested property.
predicates.compensation_recovery_not_exhausted: The creditor has not yet exhausted recovery through the compensation payable in place of the secured property.

issues.definition: When a creditor seeks to enforce a conditional personal mortgage decree, all the mortgaged estate has vested, a compensation claim has been determined, and recovery through that compensation remains incomplete, personal execution must wait until recovery through the security is pursued.
